title: WTF Happened to Toys"R"Us?
description:
For decades Toys"R"Us was every kid's favourite store. Then a giant buyout loaded it with debt, and in 2018 its US stores closed for good. Here's what really happened.

(Numbers are rounded from news reports; verify before publishing.)

scenes.heading: The Toy Kingdom
scenes.text: For generations of kids, there was no better place on earth. Toys"R"Us had aisles of toys stretching as far as you could see, and a giant flagship store right in Times Square.
Its mascot, Geoffrey the giraffe, was as famous as the toys themselves. For decades it was the biggest toy retailer in America.

scenes.heading: The Buyout
scenes.text: Then, in 2005, three investment firms bought the company for about six point six billion dollars. But most of that price was paid with borrowed money, and the debt was placed on Toys"R"Us itself.
That left the company owing around five billion dollars, with roughly four hundred million dollars a year going just to interest.
Money that could have gone into better stores and online shopping went to lenders instead. Meanwhile, Amazon and Walmart kept getting stronger.

scenes.heading: The End
scenes.text: In 2017, Toys"R"Us filed for bankruptcy. A few months later, it announced that all of its American stores would close. Closing-sale signs went up across the country.
The lesson? A company can be loved by millions of customers and still fail, if it carries more debt than it can ever pay back.
